§ 89.8

(c) *Military Representative to the DoDEA Committee.* Membership of the DoDEA Committee will include a representative from one of the Military Services to represent all four Services. OASI/MAM or OASI/MAM will nominate a representative on a rotational basis who will be designated for a 2-year term by the DAIS/MAM/EP.

(d) *Ex-Officio Member Serving as Liaison to MIC3.* In accordance with section 3-261 of DoDI 5500.07-R, the ex-officio member to the Commission, must:
(1) Be a military member or a civilian employee of DoD who can remain in the position for at least two years with a direct interface with DoDEA and the U.S. public education system as part of official duties; or
(2) Attend as a liaison meetings of MIC3, its Executive Committee, and other standing committees where requested by the Commission; or
(3) Only represent DoD interests (not the interests of MIC3), and consequently may:
(1) Engage in management or control of MIC3 (therefore, may not vote or make decisions on daily administration of MIC3);
(2) Endorse or allow the appraisal of DoD interests, events, programs, services, or enter contracts;
(3) Represent the Commission to third parties; or
(4) Represent MIC3 to the U.S. government, as prohibited by criminal statutes.
(4) Make clear to MIC3 that:
(1) The opinions expressed by the Commission do not bind DoD and/or DoD Component to any action.
(5) If included on MIC3 Web sites, all references to the incumbent by name or title must indicate that they are "DoD Ex-Officio Member" as opposed to a MIC3 member.
(5) Notify the chain of command of issues requiring policy decisions or actions requested of DoD.

§ 89.8 *Compact provisions.*

(a) *DoDEA Area School Districts Relationship With SEAs or LEAs in Member States.*

32 CFR Ch. I (7-1-24 Edition)

(1) For the purposes of DoD's implementation of the Compact in the schools it operates, DoDEA is area of offices (DoDDSS-Europe, DoDDS-Pacific, and DDESS) and their schools are considered as the equivalent of LEAs and SEAs, respectively.
(2) Each DoDEA area act as the "receiving LEA" and "sending LEA" in DoDDS-Europe. DoDEA's duties under this section will reciprocate the duties assumed by State LEAs or SEAs to children of military families, as expressed by their respective State Implementations of the Compact. Articles IV through VII DoDEA will implement the provisions described below, which, in facilitating the intent of the Compact, have been modified in the DoDEA context.
(3) *Article IV: Education Records and Enrollment—(1) Unofficial or "Hand-Carried" Education Records.* (A) If official education records cannot be released to the parents for transfer, the DoDEA custodian of the records, as the sending LEA, will attempt to provide to the parent a complete set of unofficial education records.
(B) Upon receipt of the unofficial education records, the DoDEA school, in the receiving State, shall enroll and appropriately place the child as quickly as possible based on information in the unofficial records, pending validation by the official records.
(C) *Official education records or transcripts.* (A) The DoDEA school, acting as the receiving LEA, shall request the official education record from the school in the sending State at the same time as DoDEA school enrolls and/or places the child.
(B) Upon receipt of the request for a child's records, the DoDEA school, in the sending LEA, will provide the child's official education records to the school in the receiving State, within 10 days. If there is a designated school staff break, records will be provided as soon as possible; however, the time will not exceed 10 work days after
